title: Bicolouring Steiner triple systems (Colbourn–Dinitz–Rosa product, Dinitz–Stinson conditions)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the product theorem of Colbourn, Dinitz and Rosa for bicoloured Steiner triple systems and of the necessary conditions of Dinitz and Stinson. A bicolouring of an STS colours the points so that every block receives exactly two colours. bicolourable3_mul (CDR 1999, Theorem 2.4): if there is an (a, b, c)-bicolourable STS(u) with c = max(a, b, c) and c ≤ a + b, and an (x, y, z)-bicolourable STS(v), then there is an (ax + by + cz, ay + bz + cx, az + bx + cy)-bicolourable STS(uv). Dinitz–Stinson Proposition 1.2: for a bicoloured STS on v points with colour classes of sizes c_k, 3 Σ c_k (c_k − 1) = v (v − 1) (IsSTS.three_mul_sum); no two distinct colour classes have size 2 (not_two_classes_of_size_two); and with three colour classes at most one class size is odd (Bicolourable3.not_two_odd). Four statements. The proof of Theorem 2.4 includes Lemma 2.3 of the article (forbidden latin squares exist when max(a, b, c) ≤ n/2), Ryser's theorem on completing latin arrays, and de Werra's equalized edge colourings of bipartite graphs.
